name: 9V Battery + Snap Connector
desc: A quick way to run a small Arduino project without USB (connect to VIN or the barrel jack). It drains fast, so it's not for motors or LED strips.

name: 4×AA Battery Holder (with switch)
desc: Holds four AA batteries for about 6V (or 4.8V with rechargeables). A good separate supply for servos and small motors.
note: Don't feed 6V into a board's 5V pin. Use VIN/barrel (7V+ recommended) or a regulator.

name: 5V 2A USB Wall Adapter
desc: A phone charger that powers your project through its USB cable once it no longer needs a PC.

name: 12V 2A DC Adapter (barrel jack)
desc: A wall adapter with a 5.5×2.1mm barrel plug. It powers Uno/Mega boards through their jack, plus 12V lights and motor drivers.
note: The Uno's regulator gets hot at 12V when powering extras. Fine for the board alone, but use a buck converter for bigger loads.

name: LM2596 Buck Converter (step-down)
desc: Turns a higher voltage (like 12V) into a lower one (like 5V) efficiently. Set the output with its screw before connecting anything.
note: Measure and set the output with a multimeter BEFORE connecting your board. Out of the box it can be set to anything.

name: MB102 Breadboard Power Supply
desc: Clips onto a breadboard and feeds its power rails 5V or 3.3V (a jumper picks which for each side) from a 6.5–12V adapter.
note: Check the jumper on each side before powering 3.3V-only parts.

name: TP4056 Li-ion Charger (USB-C, protected)
desc: Safely charges a single 3.7V lithium battery (18650 or LiPo) from USB. Pick the version with protection (6 pads, OUT+/OUT−).
note: Lithium cells can catch fire if shorted, punctured or wired backwards. Double-check polarity and never leave them charging unattended.

name: 5V Relay Module (1-channel)
desc: An electric switch your board can flip to turn a separate circuit on or off, like a 12V lamp or pump. It clicks!
note: Beginner rule: use it only for low-voltage DC loads (12V or less). Never wire it to 220V mains. Many modules are active-LOW (LOW = ON).

warn.3.3: Many 5V relay modules don't switch reliably from a 3.3V pin. Look for one marked "3.3V/5V trigger" or drive the input through a transistor.

name: USB Power Bank
desc: Your phone's power bank can run most projects for hours through the USB cable. The easiest portable power there is.
note: Some power banks switch off when a project draws very little current.

name: 18650 Li-ion Cell (3.7V)
desc: A rechargeable lithium cell (like a big AA) holding 2000–3000mAh. The heart of portable projects.
note: Lithium cells can catch fire if shorted, punctured, over-charged or reversed. Use protected cells from trusted sellers, charge with a TP4056 and never leave them charging unattended.

name: 18650 Battery Holder (1 cell)
desc: Holds one 18650 cell with wires for your project.
note: Check the polarity marks every time you insert a cell.

name: 18650 Battery Holder (2 in series)
desc: Holds two 18650 cells in series for about 7.4V (8.4V full). Great power for robot cars.
note: Charge each cell with a proper charger. This holder doesn't protect the cells.

name: LiPo Battery 3.7V 1000mAh (with protection)
desc: A thin, light rechargeable battery for wearables and small gadgets.
note: Don't bend, puncture or short it. Charge with a TP4056 or a board with a LiPo charger. Check the JST connector polarity before plugging in!

name: MT3608 Boost Converter (step-up)
desc: Raises a low voltage (like a 3.7V battery) to a higher one (like 5V or 12V). Set the output with its screw first.
note: Measure and set the output with a multimeter BEFORE connecting your project.

name: 5V USB Boost Module (1–5V in)
desc: Turns 1–2 AA batteries or a lithium cell into USB 5V to run a board.
note: Small boost modules give only a few hundred mA from 1–2 AA cells.

name: AMS1117 3.3V Regulator Module
desc: Turns 5V into a clean 3.3V (up to ~800mA) for ESP-01s, radios and 3.3V sensors.

name: LM7805 5V Linear Regulator
desc: The classic 3-pin regulator: feed it 7–35V, get a steady 5V (up to 1A).
note: Needs a 0.33µF capacitor on the input and 0.1µF on the output. It gets hot when the voltage drop is large: add a heatsink.

name: MP1584 Mini Buck Converter
desc: A tiny, efficient step-down module: 12V in, 5V out for your board.
note: Set the output voltage with a multimeter before connecting anything.

name: DC Barrel Jack Breakout (5.5x2.1mm)
desc: A socket for wall adapters with screw terminals, so you can feed adapter power to a breadboard.
note: Centre pin is usually +. Check with a multimeter.

name: USB-C Power Breakout (5V)
desc: Get 5V from any USB-C charger into your breadboard or project.
note: Pick one with two 5.1kΩ CC resistors, otherwise USB-C-to-C chargers won't give power.

name: 5V 4A DC Adapter (barrel jack)
desc: A strong 5V supply for LED strips and matrices.

name: 9V 1A DC Adapter (barrel jack)
desc: The ideal adapter for an Uno or Mega's barrel jack (the onboard regulator stays cooler than at 12V).

name: 5V Relay Module (2-channel)
desc: Two relays on one board, to switch two low-voltage circuits independently.
note: Beginner rule: low-voltage DC loads only, never mains. Usually active-LOW. JD-VCC jumper: leave it on unless you know why to remove it.

warn.3.3: Many 5V relay modules don't switch reliably from 3.3V pins. Use a 3.3V-trigger relay or a transistor.

name: D4184 MOSFET Switch Module
desc: A ready-made MOSFET switch board with screw terminals for LED strips, pumps and fans.
note: For motors/pumps, still add a flyback diode (1N4007) across the load.

warn.3.3: From a 3.3V pin the D4184 is only partly on: fine for loads up to ~2A, but it heats up with bigger loads.

name: Solar Panel 6V 1W
desc: A small panel that makes up to ~170mA in full sun, enough to charge a battery for outdoor sensors.
note: Use it to charge a battery through a charger module, not to power a board directly.

name: CR2032 Coin Cell Holder
desc: Holds a 3V coin cell for tiny LED gifts and RTC backups.
note: A coin cell can light an LED but can't power a board for long. Keep cells away from small children.

name: Rocker Switch (DC, panel mount)
desc: An on/off switch for the outside of your project box.
note: Beginner rule: use it only on low-voltage DC (e.g. battery or 12V adapter side), never on mains wiring.

name: Inline Fuse Holder + Blade Fuses
desc: Protects battery and 12V projects: if something shorts, the fuse blows instead of wires melting.
note: Pick a fuse rating just above your project's normal current.
